commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after alloc failure

If memory allocation fails and the resulting coder state is reused,
ensure that memory allocation is attempted again. However, coders that
are initialized via lzma_next_filter_init() shouldn't be reinitialized
after failure; they should be cleaned up with lzma_next_end().

dict_repeat() on the SSE2 path reads and writes at most 32 bytes past
the requested length. Reserve that padding at the allocation site so it
does not disappear in a build where LZ_DICT_EXTRA is 0.

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/liblzma/lz/lz_decoder.c b/src/liblzma/lz/lz_decoder.c
index 6dc4cef..020fbce 100644
--- a/src/liblzma/lz/lz_decoder.c
+++ b/src/liblzma/lz/lz_decoder.c
@@ -281,12 +281,13 @@ lzma_lz_decoder_init(lzma_next_coder *next, const lzma_allocator *allocator,
 		coder->dict.size = 0;
 		lzma_free(coder->dict.buf, allocator);
 
-		// The LZ_DICT_EXTRA bytes at the end of the buffer aren't
-		// included in alloc_size. These extra bytes allow
-		// dict_repeat() to read and write more data than requested.
-		// Otherwise this extra space is ignored.
-		coder->dict.buf = lzma_alloc(alloc_size + LZ_DICT_EXTRA,
-				allocator);
+		// The bytes at the end of the buffer aren't included in
+		// alloc_size. dict_repeat() with the SSE2 copier reads and
+		// writes at most 32 bytes more than requested; reserve that
+		// explicitly so the padding does not collapse to zero in a
+		// build where LZ_DICT_EXTRA is 0. Otherwise this extra space
+		// is ignored.
+		coder->dict.buf = lzma_alloc(alloc_size + 32, allocator);
 		if (coder->dict.buf == NULL)
 			return LZMA_MEM_ERROR;

commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Make lzma_simple_coder_init() reinit-safe after alloc failure

lzma_raw_coder_init() always calls lzma_next_end() if an error occurs
in filter initialization, and no other code path can call
lzma_simple_coder_init(), so this change doesn't fix any bug.
This is just to reduce likelyhood of future bugs.

Also copy 64 bytes per iteration in the SSE2 dict_repeat(). The extra
bytes are covered by LZ_DICT_EXTRA, which is raised to 64 to match.
LZ_DICT_REPEAT_MAX stays 288, still enough for the longest LZMA match.

coupling: 250ab9a spells the SSE2 dictionary-tail padding out as a literal 32, which matches dict_repeat() at that commit: the copier still moves 32 bytes and LZ_DICT_EXTRA is still 32, so the allocation is unchanged for every build that actually uses the SSE2 path. 150799a widens the SSE2 loop to 64-byte loads and stores and raises LZ_DICT_EXTRA from 32 to 64, so any allocation that still adds the macro stays ahead of the new overshoot; that commit does not touch lz_decoder.c. Each diff is internally consistent (32-byte copies with 32 bytes of tail, or 64-byte copies with a 64-byte macro). The heap overflow appears only when the hardcoded 32-byte allocation is combined with the 64-byte copier: a match whose remaining length is not a multiple of 64, issued when the write cursor is within 32 bytes of the end of the dictionary buffer, stores past the allocation. Reverting only the literal in 250ab9a makes the allocation follow LZ_DICT_EXTRA again (64 on the widened tree); reverting only the chunk size in 150799a puts the copier back to 32 bytes. Either of those is safe, but it is not a local property of one diff: the constant each commit introduces is justified only by the code the other commit changes, so a correct repair has to look at both.
